dimensions.assessment: Affects federal land management agencies, Indian Tribes, Alaska Native and Native Hawaiian organizations, and state and local governments.
dimensions.evidence: outreach to--(1) Indian Tribes; (2) States; (3) territories; (4) units of local government; (5) Alaska Native organizations

dimensions.assessment: Establishes a structured program to identify, prioritize, and fund post-disaster ecosystem restoration and seed availability projects.
dimensions.evidence: carry out priority projects through--(A) competitively awarded grants; (B) contracts; (C) contracts established under the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes grants, contracts, and cooperative agreements for priority projects and seed availability, but does not explicitly state a total funding authorization amount.
dimensions.evidence: opportunities to establish dedicated funding necessary to address any backlog of reforestation and restoration needs.

dimensions.assessment: Creates a new multi-agency program led by the Secretary of the Interior covering federal lands and Indian Forest Land or Rangeland.
dimensions.evidence: require the Secretary of the Interior to carry out a program for Post-Disaster Reforestation and Restoration Program

dimensions.assessment: Includes a sunset provision terminating authority 7 years after the date of enactment, alongside ongoing annual reporting requirements.
dimensions.evidence: The authority provided under this section shall terminate on the date that is 7 years after the date of enactment of this Act.

missing_information: Specific funding amounts or appropriation caps for the grant and contract programs are not provided in the text.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill directs the Department of the Interior to establish an annual post-disaster reforestation and restoration program for federal and tribal lands, supported by grants, contracts, and outreach.
